text:
ava: heads up — customer on macOS arm64 (ventura) sees build from sdist when installing via poetry, and the build fails during the binary extension compile step.

ava: log:
```
Building wheel for redwood-sdk (pyproject.toml) ...
  error: command '/usr/bin/clang' failed with exit code 1
  
  note: wheel for platform macosx_11_0_arm64 not found; sdist being built instead
```

chris: looks like we never published a universal2 or macosx_arm64 wheel for the native extension. our cibuildwheel config only targeted manylinux and x86_64 macos.

leo: also noticed poetry creates a lockfile with platform markers and pins `httpx[http2]` to 0.23.x from one of our extras — on arm64 that led to a transitive dependency that needs a binary (h11) build which then fails.

chris: two immediate fixes: publish macos universal2 and arm64 wheels, and make the httpx extra optional and lightweight (document `redwood-sdk[async]`). currently async support pulls httpx by default and that confuses poetry resolver.

ava: workaround for customer: in CI use `poetry install --no-dev --no-root --extras "async"` or export requirements: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes --extras async | pip install -r -` — that avoids poetry rebuilding sdist locally.

pip-bot: FYI: recent pip >=23.2 supports macosx_11_0_arm64 tags better; recommend adding a note in install docs to upgrade pip when using poetry on macOS.

leo: small packaging RFC: split platform-specific compiled bits into an optional package (redwood-sdk-native) so main wheel stays pure-python and always has a wheel on PyPI. then provide redwood-sdk[fast] to pull native.

ops: can we also add `py.typed` and ship stubs for AsyncClient? a typed wheel reduces friction for typed codebases.

chris: agreed. I'll open PRs: 1) cibuildwheel matrix to include macos_arm64 + universal2 + aarch64 manylinux; 2) change extras to `redwood-sdk[async]` and make httpx optional; 3) add py.typed + minimal .pyi for AsyncClient.

ava: thanks — passing workaround to customer, and we'll track the PRs. :thumbsup:
